item.title: In 2013, Florida’s Tortuga Music Festival began restoring dunes with sea oats; 13 years later...
item.description: For over thirteen years, music enthusiasts and dedicated volunteers have joined forces to rejuvenate the dunes at Fort Lauderdale Beach, a tradition that began alongside the Tortuga Music Festival in 2013. By planting resilient sea oats, they bolster coastal defenses against storm surges and erosion, while also creating essential nesting grounds for sea turtles. This inspiring initiative exemplifies how large-scale public events can embrace sustainability. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Astronomers hear a mysterious cosmic hum linked to strange dark stars from 13 billion years ago
item.description: Astronomers may have found a new way to investigate the Universe's first supermassive black holes. A faint gravitational-wave hum detected through pulsars could contain clues about ancient objects. Hypothetical Dark Stars, powered partly by dark matter, could have left black-hole descendants. These ancient black-hole seeds could grow and merge, producing part of the gravitational-wave background. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Northern spotted owl once became a symbol of America’s logging wars; now scientists say it is already functionally extinct
item.description: The northern spotted owl, once a revered icon of environmental activism, faces dire circumstances as it becomes functionally extinct in numerous regions. A recent study indicates a severe decline in its populations throughout their historical habitat. Factors such as habitat destruction and rampant wildfires have severely impacted the species over the years, while the encroaching barred owl emerges as a formidable threat. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
